scope: Error/usage logging for a 2-user hobby app: Cloudflare Worker (Hono) + D1 on the API side, SvelteKit PWA on the web side. Prices are USD, current as of 2026-11-22.

included: Datadog Free plan is separate from the trial; it is an infrastructure-metrics tier, not a logs or APM tier.
limits: APM is NOT included on the free plan (paid APM starts at $31/host/month, billed annually).
Log Management is NOT included on the free plan; log retention is not part of free.
Only 1 day of metric retention, so no useful history or long-term trend analysis.

The '5 hosts' model fits servers/VMs/containers, not Cloudflare Workers. Serverless/Workers monitoring is metered separately by usage, so the free host allowance does not cleanly cover a Worker + D1 + PWA stack.
Only 5 hosts means a hobby app with real log volume quickly leaves the free tier once you need logs or APM.
Product breadth (Logs, APM, RUM, Synthetics) is billed per product on top of Infrastructure, so a 'free' hobby stack realistically becomes multiple paid SKUs.
datadog_free_tier.entry_paid_cost: Infrastructure Monitoring Pro from $15/host/month (annual) or $18 on-demand; APM from $31/host/month (annual); Log Management ingest from $0.10/GB/month, plus indexing (e.g. $1.70 per million log events at 15-day retention; retention tiers of 3, 7, 15, 30 days). Flex Storage retention starts at 1 month ($0.05 per million events stored). A free trial is offered (length not stated on the pricing page).
datadog_free_tier.verdict: Datadog's free tier is an infrastructure-metrics tier (5 hosts, 1-day retention) and does NOT include log management or APM, so it cannot deliver free error/usage logging for this project. Turning on logs or APM moves the bill to per-host (APM $15-31/host/month) plus per-GB log ingest/indexing, and the host model maps poorly to Workers. Datadog is the wrong fit and the most expensive option here; skip it for a 2-user hobby app.

cloudflare_native.name: Cloudflare Workers Logs (Workers Observability)
cloudflare_native.cost: Free plan: 200,000 log events/day included, 3-day retention. Workers Paid ($5/month min): 20 million events/month included, then $0.60 per additional million, 7-day retention. From 2026-12-01 it moves to Cloudflare Observability pricing: Free 0.5 GB/day ingestion with 7-day retention (ingestion stops at the daily cap); Paid 50 GB/cycle ingestion + 10 GB-month storage included, then $0.25/GB ingest and $0.10/GB-month storage.
cloudflare_native.captures: Automatic invocation logs (request, response, metadata), all console.log/custom logs (JSON is parsed and indexed for filtering), console errors, uncaught exceptions. Pair with Workers Issues to group and alert on failures (5xx, uncaught exceptions, error-level logs). Supports head-based sampling and source maps for readable stack traces.
cloudflare_native.setup: Lowest effort. Set observability.enabled = true in the Worker's wrangler config (on by default for new Workers) and redeploy. View in dashboard under the Worker > Observability.

cloudflare_native.name: Cloudflare Logpush (Workers Trace Events + HTTP Requests) to R2/S3/etc.
cloudflare_native.cost: Logpush on Free/Pro/Business is usage-based: 25 GB/account/month included; internal destinations (R2, Pipelines) $0.03/GB after that, external destinations $0.10/GB, transformation $0.04/GB. Workers Trace Events Logpush requires the Workers Paid plan: 10 million requests/month included, then $0.05 per additional million. Destination storage is billed separately (R2: 10 GB-month free tier, then $0.015/GB-month).
cloudflare_native.captures: Full field-level records (HTTP Requests ~1.5-3 kB/record; Workers Trace Events with console logs, exceptions, outcome) delivered near real time as gzip batches to R2, S3, or a SIEM/provider.
cloudflare_native.retention: None at Cloudflare; you own retention at the destination (e.g. R2 lifecycle rules).
cloudflare_native.setup: Medium. Create a Logpush job via dashboard/API and provision a destination bucket (e.g. R2). Caveat: no backfill, logs during a disabled/failed job are lost, so configure health notifications.

cloudflare_native.name: Tail Workers
cloudflare_native.cost: Requires Workers Paid (or Enterprise). Billed by CPU time, not by request count (no per-request charge).
cloudflare_native.captures: Per-invocation execution data about a producer Worker: HTTP status, console.log output, uncaught exceptions, and diagnostics-channel events. You forward them anywhere over HTTP.
cloudflare_native.retention: None by itself; retention depends on whatever endpoint/store you forward to (KV, D1, R2, third party).
cloudflare_native.setup: Medium-high. Create a Worker with a tail() handler, add it to the producer Worker's tail_consumers, then handle/forward events yourself. Documented as the 'advanced mode' for custom needs; for standard error/log export Cloudflare recommends OpenTelemetry export instead.

cloudflare_native.name: Workers Analytics Engine
cloudflare_native.cost: Free plan: 100,000 data points/day + 10,000 read queries/day. Workers Paid: 10 million data points/month + 1 million read queries/month, then $0.25/additional million writes and $1.00/additional million reads. Cloudflare currently does not bill for Analytics Engine; pricing is published in advance for future billing.
cloudflare_native.captures: Custom high-cardinality time-series metrics written from Worker code via writeDataPoint() (blobs, doubles, indexes), queried with SQL (SQL API). It is aggregated metrics/usage analytics, not raw log storage.
cloudflare_native.retention: Approximately 90 days (fixed Cloudflare retention window; not user-configurable).
cloudflare_native.setup: Medium. Bind a dataset to the Worker, call writeDataPoint in code paths, and query via the SQL API or Grafana/dashboard. Good for usage counters and per-endpoint error rates, not for reading individual log lines.

third_party.name: Sentry
third_party.cost_free_tier: Developer plan: $0, 1 user, 5,000 errors/month, 5 GB logs, 5 GB app metrics, 5M spans, 50 replays, 1 uptime/cron monitor, 10 dashboards. Paid entry: Team $26/month.
third_party.captures: Error monitoring with stack traces, tracing, logs, session replays, app metrics, cron/uptime monitors. Has a Cloudflare Workers SDK (@sentry/cloudflare).
third_party.retention: 30-day lookback on free; up to 90 days on paid.
third_party.setup: Low-medium. Install @sentry/cloudflare, wrap the Worker handler withSentry(), and upload source maps. Best-in-class error grouping and alerting for the price.

third_party.name: Axiom
third_party.cost_free_tier: Personal plan: $0/month, permanent, no credit card. 500 GB/month data loading compute, 10 GB-hours query compute, 25 GB storage, 30-day retention, full query language (APL), all integrations. Paid: Axiom Cloud $25/month platform fee + usage.
third_party.captures: Logs, traces, and metrics via OpenTelemetry, Vector, CloudWatch, and other integrations; SQL/APL querying, dashboards, alerts.
third_party.setup: Medium. Send Cloudflare Worker logs/traces via the built-in OpenTelemetry export or a Vector/HTTP source. Generous free allowance for a hobby app.

third_party.name: Grafana Cloud
third_party.cost_free_tier: Free forever: 50 GB logs/month, 50 GB traces/month, 10k metrics active series, 3 Grafana users, 14-day retention, community support. Paid: Pro from $19/month + usage (30-day logs retention, 13-month metrics).
third_party.captures: Logs (Loki), traces (Tempo), metrics (Prometheus), profiles, plus dashboards/alerting, synthetic monitoring, RUM.
third_party.setup: Medium-high. Wire Cloudflare (OpenTelemetry export or Loki push) and learn the Grafana stack. Powerful but heavier than needed for two users.

third_party.name: Better Stack
third_party.cost_free_tier: Free for personal projects: 10 monitors & heartbeats, 1 status page, 100,000 exceptions/month, 5,000 session replays, 3 GB logs retained 3 days, 3 GB traces retained 3 days, 30 GB metrics. Paid entry: Nano bundle from $30/month (EU) or $45/month (US) with 30-day retention; usage beyond is metered per GB.
third_party.captures: Logs, traces, metrics, error tracking (Sentry-SDK compatible), uptime/heartbeat monitoring, session replay, status pages, on-call/incident management.
third_party.setup: Medium. Point logs at a Better Stack source (HTTP/Vector/OTel); error tracking reuses a Sentry-compatible SDK. Free log retention is only 3 days.

third_party.name: Baselime
third_party.cost_free_tier: No longer an independent product. Cloudflare acquired Baselime (announced 2024) and folded its technology into Cloudflare's own observability (OpenTelemetry-based Workers Observability). Existing Baselime users kept access during transition; new projects should use Cloudflare Workers Logs / OTel export instead.
third_party.captures: Historically: OpenTelemetry logs/traces/metrics and real-time error tracking for serverless.
third_party.retention: N/A as a standalone option; see Cloudflare Workers Logs and Cloudflare Observability pricing.
third_party.setup: Not applicable for new work; not a separate free-tier vendor anymore.

recommendation.for_this_project: Use Cloudflare Workers Logs as the primary logging layer, and add Sentry's free Developer plan only if you want grouped error tracking with a nicer UI and 30-day history. Skip Datadog entirely.
recommendation.why: Workers Logs is native, needs a one-line wrangler change, and its free allowance (200,000 log events/day, 3-day retention) is far more than a 2-user hobby app generates. It captures exactly what you care about (invocation logs, console.log, errors, uncaught exceptions) and Workers Issues adds failure alerting at no cost. If 3-day retention or a dedicated error UI becomes a limitation, Sentry free (5k errors/month, 30-day lookback, 1 user, Workers SDK) is the cheapest upgrade; Axiom Personal (25 GB storage, 30-day, $0) is the alternative if you want a log-search/query experience. Datadog is the worst fit: its free tier covers only 1-day infrastructure metrics with no logs or APM, and real log/APM usage is $15-31/host/month plus per-GB ingest.
steps: 1. In each Worker's wrangler config add observability = { enabled = true } (or JSON observability: { enabled: true }) and redeploy. New Workers have this on by default.

2. Log structured JSON from the API and PWA (e.g. console.error({ event, status, route, userId, requestId })) so Workers Logs indexes fields for filtering; use console.error for handled failures so Workers Issues groups them.
3. Enable Workers Issues and create an automation/webhook (or a Monitors threshold query on logs.workersLogs) to alert on 5xx and uncaught exceptions with an occurrence threshold of 1.
4. Upload build source maps (framework builds must generate and upload them) so exception stacks point to original files and lines.

5. Optional, only if you need longer than 3-day retention: create a Logpush job to an R2 bucket (25 GB/month free across internal destinations; R2 has a 10 GB-month free tier) and set an R2 lifecycle rule. Logpush has no backfill, so enable health notifications.

6. Optional, if you want grouped errors with 30-day history and email alerts: add @sentry/cloudflare to the API Worker on the free Developer plan, wrap the handler with withSentry(), and upload source maps.
7. Do not sign up for Datadog for this project; the free tier does not include logs or APM and the entry cost is per-host plus per-GB.
